_comment: TARGET-tier scope definition for a WRAP-ONLY campaign over libxml2
v2.15.3. There is no port scope: nothing is translated to native Rust.
The deliverable is a safe Rust wrapper over the whole published C API,
so the target is defined by the headers that publish it.
_comment_files: `files.port` is empty, and that is the point. Every entity classifies
wrap, no C source is fenced or re-exported, and libxml2 builds
unmodified - Rust links the existing shared object.
`files.wrap` anchors the public header directory. Every function,
global and type declared under include/libxml/ enters the wrap surface
directly, independent of whether anything in this target reaches it -
which is the only way in when there is no port scope to seed a closure.
45 headers, 1416 XMLPUBFUN declarations at this tag.
The definitions are all present in the CodeQL database (55 .c files at
the repo root, one shared object) even though none of them is ported.
That is what the ownership analysis walks: free / store / return paths
read off the real implementation rather than guessed from a signature,
which is the thing a hand-written -sys crate cannot do.
A struct DEFINED in one of these headers is a value type whose fields
are the API, so its field types are walked in full. One merely
forward-declared there stays an opaque handle. libxml2 defines most of
its tree structs publicly (xmlNode, xmlDoc, xmlAttr), so the value-type
share here is far higher than in OpenSSL.
NOT anchored, deliberately: the private headers under include/private/
and the two repo-root headers (libxml.h, timsort.h). They declare
libxml2's internals, which no consumer includes; anything the public
API genuinely exposes from them reaches wrap scope through the type
closure instead, and lands as an opaque handle.
_comment_out_of_scope: `paths` is empty. The candidates are excluded by construction: `files`
names only include/libxml/, so test/, fuzz/, python/, example/ and the
xmllint/xmlcatalog programs are outside it and never enter.
`features` is documentation only - no composer reads it. It lists the
LIBXML2_WITH_* options that are OFF in the configure line recorded in
build.json, so a body they elide contributes no entities and drops out
